I've run into a bit of a snag, and was hoping someone in here might be able to help me.

As the title suggests, I have a network game where my bullets are controlled by the server. Everything works great, except interpolation.

Now, on my units, I have a NetworkRigidbody component that is able to do extrapolation/interpolation on networked rigidbodies. This works by storing roughly 20 states for position/rotation/velocity.

My problem is that I can't use the same method for bullets, as they are 1) pooled objects and 2) bullets have no prior states when being initialized.

So how do I work around that - how do I create the states, back in time, when neither the server, or client actually knows where the bullet has been the last ~20 states?

The end result at the moment is that bullets on clients will appear to be a few frames ahead, because they cannot account for any previous positions/states the bullet might have.

Thanks in advance :)

While I have a first-person-like game I'm working on, I don't have any bullets, so I'm probably not the best person to answer this. But I do like to help people work through their problems, so I'll help while I can.

If you want to use the same code and just need ~20 prior states, there are some options. Say, if you use the gun's local "forward" to orient the bullet, you can use the "backward" to get the opposite direction and simply generate some points a few time steps backwards.

Thanks for chiming in :)

I see what you're getting at, but unfortunately it would not work in this scenario.

All bullets here are managed by the server, as the position of bullets in this game is pretty important (to be able to avoid missiles and whatnot). So, whenever a unit attacks, the client doesn't actually do anything, whereas the server initializes the bullet and informs the clients.

So, lets say a client is flying along its forward axis at 1 meter per second and starts to attack. The client's position is always a bit behind the server due to the interpolation/extrapolation in the NetworkRigidbody, so when the server initializes the bullet, it gets initialized at the position where the server sees the client, but that position does not correlate with the position on the client, as the client is in the past. But the bullet itself has no previous states to interpolate/extrapolate from, as it was just fired. Even if I stored 20 states with the same position/rotation and sent them to the client, the stored states would still be "in the future" as far as the client is concerned.

Do you have time stamps on the history of the ship? Could you fire the bullet at the position the ship was in half of the NetworkTransport.GetCurrentRtt? As in, half of the round trip time was approximately when the player fired the bullet.

Should probably mention that I'm using RakNet (Unity 4.6), so a lot of the nice new network features are not available to me.

But yes, the ship states have timestamps that, technically, could be tapped into - but that could get really messy.

All bullets are handled by a "manager"/object pool, that the server takes control of when a client connects. Everything there is serialized through OnSerializeNetworkView().

I guess what you are suggesting is, that I just send the id of the bullet-owner's ship to the clients and offset the bullet's position with a vector like (ship.transform.position - ship.networkStates[0].position)?

That is what I'm suggesting (just sending the ID of player to a fire command on the server), but it would be nicer if you could use the real position from the networkStates array instead of using [0].

I don't know RakNet, but hopefully they have some kind of round-trip-time that you can access or implement (I see those words in the documentation, but it means nothing to me). You'd also need to save the time in the networkStates class. Then you could use half the RTT as an estimate as to when the player pressed their fire key and use linear interpolation between networkStates to estimate where the ship was back then.

(I'm still just guessing. Sorry if I'm not helping.)
